editorial:
Imagine being fifteen years old, weighing barely a hundred pounds, and feeling like the world is against you. That is exactly where you find Michael Peck. He is a baby-faced high school sophomore who just cannot catch a break. Between teachers who treat him like he is slow and classmates who see him as a total geek, his school life is a nightmare. To make things worse, his parents are way too strict. They actually use planners to schedule family time and make him sign legal contracts just to do after-school activities. It is a funny but sad look at what it feels like to be the underdog in a place where everyone wants you to fit in.

You will really enjoy how the movie captures those awkward teen years without getting too heavy. The acting feels natural, and the pacing keeps you interested as you root for Peck to finally win. While some of the jokes are a bit simple, the heart of the story is what makes it work. It is a perfect pick for a cozy weekend in with the family.
endingExplained: By the end, Peck finally finds his voice and stops letting others push him around. He learns that he does not need to fit the mold of the cool kids to be happy. He manages to stand up to his overly organized parents, leading them to relax their strict rules. The movie wraps up with Peck gaining a new level of confidence and respect from his peers, proving that being yourself is the best way to survive high school.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories and underdog triumphs.
